copierUpdate.description: Identifies the template and the version range being applied, i.e. the answers-file `_src_path` and the old/new `_commit`.

answers_changed.description: Answer keys whose values changed as part of this update, excluding `_commit`.

answers_file.description: Path to the answers file this update is driven by.

cli_flags.description: Extra flags passed to copier, e.g. '--skip-answered', '--trust'.

conflict_mode.description: Copier's --conflict setting: 'rej' writes .rej files, 'inline' writes conflict markers into the file.

copier_version.description: Version of the copier CLI that performed the update.

from_commit.description: Template commit behind from_version, when the tag alone is not enough to reproduce the diff.

from_version.description: Template version the project was previously generated or updated from (the old `_commit`), usually a git tag.

to_version.description: Template version being updated to (the new `_commit`).

allOf.description: A rejected patch must carry the .rej contents.
Anything not fully resolved must be flagged for review.
A rejected hunk still pending must be flagged for review.
Retained conflict markers must be flagged for review.

fileResolution.description: How the conflicts in one file were resolved.

confidence.description: How confident the resolver is that this resolution is correct.

conflict_markers_retained.description: True if conflict markers (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) are still present in the working-tree file.

conflict_type.description: Nature of the conflict as git reported it.

description.description: What was resolved: the conflicting change on each side and what the final content ended up being.
examples: Both branches added a `timeout` argument to `run_protocol()`. Kept theirs (keyword-only, default 300s) and applied our docstring wording on top.

filename.description: Repository-relative path of the conflicted file, POSIX separators, no leading './'.

is_answers_file.description: True for the Copier answers file itself (e.g. .copier-answers.yml), which conflicts on almost every update and is normally resolved by keeping the new _commit plus our answer values.

needs_review.description: True if a human should verify this file before the result is merged or pushed.

reason.description: Why this resolution was chosen over the alternatives — the decision rationale, not a restatement of the change.
examples: Their signature is already consumed by two callers on main; ours was only used in the test added in this branch, so adopting theirs avoids a follow-up API break.

rej_file.description: The .rej artifact produced by `git apply`/`patch` for this file, captured verbatim.

related_issues.description: Issue or ticket keys relevant to the decision, e.g. Jira keys.

renamed_from.description: Previous path, when the conflict involved a rename or move.

resolution_strategy.description: Which side(s) the resolved content came from.

template_path.description: Path of the source file inside the Copier template that generated this file, including the .jinja suffix if present.

verification.description: Evidence that the resolution actually works.

commands.description: Commands run to verify the resolved file, e.g. 'pytest tests/test_plate_mapper.py'.

rejFile.description: A .rej reject file captured as-is. `contents` is the literal file text; do not reflow, re-indent, or strip trailing whitespace, since patch context depends on it.

byte_size.description: Size of the original .rej file in bytes, for round-trip checking.

contents.description: Raw, byte-for-byte contents of the .rej file, newlines preserved.

disposition.description: What was done about the rejected hunks.

encoding.description: How `contents` is encoded. Use 'base64' for non-UTF-8 or binary rejects.

hunk_count.description: Number of rejected hunks in the file.

path.description: Path of the .rej file on disk, typically '<filename>.rej'.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the original .rej file bytes.

truncated.description: True if `contents` holds only part of the .rej file.

allOf.description: A Copier operation must record which template versions it spans.

description: A record of how conflicts were resolved during a `copier update` (or a plain git merge/rebase). One report covers a single update and contains one entry per conflicted file.

commits.description: The commits this update made on top of project_commit, newest first: the update commit and any fix commits. `report` fills it in from git when the draft leaves it out.

copier.description: Template identity and the version range this update spans. Required when operation is copier-update or copier-recopy.

operation.description: The operation that produced the conflicts.

project.description: The project being updated (repo remote URL, or a name like 'example-org/example-project').

project_commit.description: State of the project repo the update was applied on top of.

resolved_by.description: Who or what resolved the conflicts, e.g. 'a.developer@example.com' or 'claude-opus-5'.

summary.description: Optional one-paragraph overview of the whole operation.

title: Copier Update Conflict Resolution Report
